title: Extremely Fast and Accurate Transcription with Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC
gist: IBM released two compact 470M-parameter Granite Speech 5.0 encoder-only models that hit over 12,600 RTFx on an H200 GPU (3.5+ hours of audio per second), trading away speech-translation capability for a 20x throughput gain over prior Granite Speech models, with a two-tier license split (Apache 2.0 vs CC-BY-NC-SA) that carries a measurable, quantified accuracy cost.

themes.theme: Extreme throughput as the headline claim

insights.claim: IBM's new Granite Speech 5.0 models are 470M-parameter English speech recognition models achieving over 12,600 RTFx on an Nvidia H200 GPU, meaning they can transcribe more than 3.5 hours of speech in one second using batched inference.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: This throughput level sharply lowers per-hour transcription compute cost, relevant to enterprises evaluating ASR infrastructure spend for large-scale batch transcription (call centers, media archives, compliance recording review).
insights.quote: compact, 470M-parameter English speech recognition models that pair strong accuracy with unprecedented speed — over 12,600 RTFx on an NVIDIA H200 GPU, meaning they can transcribe more than 3.5 hours of speech in one second using batched inference

insights.claim: The encoder-only architecture shift gives Granite Speech 5.0 models over 20x faster throughput than prior Granite Speech models, which used a full acoustic encoder plus projector plus Granite LM with LoRA adapters.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: A >20x speed jump within the same model family in a single generation is a large efficiency leap, signaling rapid ASR cost curves are still falling even without new hardware generations.
insights.quote: The encoder-only design provides strong transcription performance, a small memory footprint of only 470M parameters, and over 20x faster throughput than previous Granite Speech models.

insights.claim: To achieve the speed gain, the models reduce their output token rate from 50 characters per second (previous encoders) to 12.5 tokens per second via three stages of 2x subsampling of the log-Mel spectrogram front end.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: The core mechanism behind the speedup (aggressive temporal subsampling) is a reusable technique other ASR vendors could adopt to chase similar throughput gains — worth watching for competitive responses.
insights.quote: While our previous encoders generated 50 characters per second, the Granite 5.0 models generate 12.5 tokens per second

insights.claim: The new encoder-only Granite Speech 5.0 models give up speech translation and keyword-biasing capabilities that the prior LM-equipped Granite Speech models had, in exchange for far lower memory footprint and higher throughput, explicitly targeting speech-to-text tasks on edge devices.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: IBM is explicitly segmenting its speech model line by use case: a smaller, faster, transcription-only tier for edge/high-throughput deployment versus a larger, more capable tier for translation/biasing use cases — a productization pattern other model families may follow.
insights.quote: The new models give up some of the capabilities of the LM-equipped models, such as speech translation and keyword biasing, but they are ideal for speech-to-text tasks on edge devices.

themes.theme: Licensing tiers carry a quantified accuracy cost

insights.claim: The non-commercial model (granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-nc, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 licensed, trained on more data) scores 4.85% aggregate word error rate versus 5.00% for the Apache 2.0 commercially-licensed model trained on less data, with the non-commercial model showing a more noticeable advantage on SPGI Speech and a disadvantage on the new chunked Earnings22 test.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: IBM is putting a concrete, measured price (0.15 WER points) on choosing permissive Apache 2.0 licensing over the non-commercial tier, giving enterprise buyers a quantified basis for the build-vs-buy licensing tradeoff.
insights.quote: the noncommercial model scoring an aggregate 4.85% WER and the Apache 2.0 model scoring 5.00% WER

insights.claim: The non-commercial model was trained on additional datasets not used for the Apache 2.0 model, including 10,000 hours of GigaSpeech and 4,900 hours of SPGI Speech, showing IBM deliberately gates certain training data behind the non-commercial license.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: This two-tier data/license structure is a template other open-model providers may use to monetize the accuracy gains from their best training data while still offering a fully open, commercially usable baseline model.

insights.claim: On the far-field speech recognition (FFASR) leaderboard, the Apache 2.0 model ranks ninth in accuracy while the non-commercial model ranks fifth while also being the fastest among the top five models on that leaderboard.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: Competitive accuracy ranking (top five/nine) combined with leading speed on FFASR demonstrates the speed gains are not purely a tradeoff against accuracy in far-field conditions, strengthening the model's competitive position versus rival open ASR models.
insights.quote: ibm-granite/granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc ranked ninth in accuracy and ibm-granite/granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-nc ranked fifth while also being the fastest two models

insights.claim: Both Granite Speech 5.0 models are trained partly on synthetic data, including 240 hours of synthetic utterances covering numbers, currencies, website names, phone numbers, and addresses, generated using the open-weight models gpt-oss-120b or gpt-oss-20b and synthesized into audio using StyleTTS2.
insights.speaker: Brian Kingsbury
insights.so_what: Shows a concrete production use of open-weight LLMs (gpt-oss) purely as synthetic-data generators to patch narrow domain gaps (numeric/entity-heavy speech) in a commercial ASR training pipeline — a pattern likely replicated across other model teams building domain-specific training data.
insights.quote: 240 hours of utterances containing numbers, currencies, website names, phone numbers, and addresses, and items containing decimal points or dots which were generated using either gpt-oss-120b or gpt-oss-20b and synthesized using StyleTTS2
